investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T09:30–09:38Z because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was left unschedulable: the 6-node Kubernetes cluster reported 2 nodes with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with no preemption victims available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state and times out before the eval runner can observe a running VM. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api environment; no eval infrastructure code change is implicated by the evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for a separate pod stuck for 147s, confirming the condition is not a transient single-pod fluke.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for a third pod stuck for 148s, confirming the exhaustion persisted across the full eval window (09:30–09:38Z).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with a pre-VM-start failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the two eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/stuck VMs from prior runs have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node selector that only matches 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity; any reduction in that node set (e.g., a node cordoned, drained, or replaced) would immediately exhaust the schedulable pool.

TERTIARY — VM leak from a previous eval run: if a prior remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state probe did not clean up its VM (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs failed silently), the leaked VM would hold a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

LOWER — cluster under-provisioning: the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a quota too small to handle concurrent eval probes for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime running in the same window.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would disprove active capacity exhaustion and suggest the failure was transient.

kubectl describe nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (allocatable > requested) on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was caused by a different constraint (e.g., a transient API server error or a race condition) rather than true exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod was scheduled but the VM failed to reach a ready state (e.g., a non-empty evidence object containing orgId and agentId but vmIdPresent=false) would shift the root cause from scheduler capacity to VM provisioning or runtime failure.
Evidence that only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed would suggest a pod-specific misconfiguration rather than cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of local-agent-create or other non-remote checks in the same eval window would confirm the failure is isolated to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class and not a broader API or authentication outage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on each eligible node and warns before the pool reaches 100% utilization.

Add a VM-leak detection eval that enumerates remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL in the production-api namespace and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's node selector, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a safe threshold.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so that future failures distinguish between capacity exhaustion, affinity mismatch, and other scheduler errors without requiring manual log inspection.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Swarm Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T09:33–09:38Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented the agent from ever being created, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) completely absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected by the scheduler with Unschedulable status, causing the pod to remain pending for ~147–148 seconds before the eval timed out. No agent was ever provisioned, so the state-polling step never ran and produced zero evidence output.

Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of overall cluster size. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — transient cluster saturation spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads may have temporarily exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run. This would be a transient condition rather than a persistent misconfiguration.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create passed, the root cause would be localized to state-polling logic rather than pod scheduling.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type exists on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node feature/label rather than exhaustion of an existing resource.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all remote-agent-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), catching topology drift before it reduces the schedulable pool to a single point of failure.

Add a stuck-pod detection eval that scans for remote agent pods in Pending/Unschedulable state older than a configurable threshold and reports them as a separate check, enabling faster triage without waiting for the full eval timeout.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent-create eval runner branch that validates node scheduling feasibility (dry-run pod scheduling) before committing to the full agent creation flow, so the failure message is captured as structured evidence rather than a raw scheduler string.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 09:33 and 09:38 UTC on 2026-06-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every eval pod that requests a remote agent VM times out unscheduled (~146–154 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream evidence collection impossible. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the kata peer-pod VM resource class have no remaining allocatable capacity, and no preemption victims exist to free slots. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. If those rules were recently tightened or if nodes were relabeled, the effective scheduling pool shrank to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, making capacity exhaustion more likely to surface.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T09:30–09:38Z because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was left unschedulable: the 6-node Kubernetes cluster reported 2 nodes with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with no preemption victims available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state and times out before the eval runner can observe a running VM. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api environment; no eval infrastructure code change is implicated by the evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for a separate pod stuck for 147s, confirming the condition is not a transient single-pod fluke.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for a third pod stuck for 148s, confirming the exhaustion persisted across the full eval window (09:30–09:38Z).
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with a pre-VM-start failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; evidence can only be written after the agent VM is live, so scheduler failure prevents any evidence from being captured.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the two eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/stuck VMs from prior runs have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node selector that only matches 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity; any reduction in that node set (e.g., a node cordoned, drained, or replaced) would immediately exhaust the schedulable pool.

TERTIARY — VM leak from a previous eval run: if a prior remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state probe did not clean up its VM (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs failed silently), the leaked VM would hold a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

LOWER — cluster under-provisioning: the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a quota too small to handle concurrent eval probes for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime running in the same window.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would disprove active capacity exhaustion and suggest the failure was transient.

kubectl describe nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (allocatable > requested) on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was caused by a different constraint (e.g., a transient API server error or a race condition) rather than true exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod was scheduled but the VM failed to reach a ready state (e.g., a non-empty evidence object containing orgId and agentId but vmIdPresent=false) would shift the root cause from scheduler capacity to VM provisioning or runtime failure.
Evidence that only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed would suggest a pod-specific misconfiguration rather than cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of local-agent-create or other non-remote checks in the same eval window would confirm the failure is isolated to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class and not a broader API or authentication outage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on each eligible node and warns before the pool reaches 100% utilization.

Add a VM-leak detection eval that enumerates remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL in the production-api namespace and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's node selector, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a safe threshold.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so that future failures distinguish between capacity exhaustion, affinity mismatch, and other scheduler errors without requiring manual log inspection.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T09:33–09:38Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod scheduling failure prevented the agent from ever being created, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) completely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected by the scheduler with Unschedulable status, causing the pod to remain pending for ~147–148 seconds before the eval timed out. No agent was ever provisioned, so the state-polling step never ran and produced zero evidence output.

If the 3 sibling checks pass on a subsequent run without any cluster changes, the failure was transient saturation rather than a persistent capacity or configuration problem.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create passed, the root cause would be localized to state-polling logic rather than pod scheduling.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod matches more than 2 nodes in the current cluster configuration, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a cluster topology change rather than a static misconfiguration.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type exists on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node feature/label rather than exhaustion of an existing resource.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all remote-agent-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), catching topology drift before it reduces the schedulable pool to a single point of failure.

Add a stuck-pod detection eval that scans for remote agent pods in Pending/Unschedulable state older than a configurable threshold and reports them as a separate check, enabling faster triage without waiting for the full eval timeout.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent-create eval runner branch that validates node scheduling feasibility (dry-run pod scheduling) before committing to the full agent creation flow, so the failure message is captured as structured evidence rather than a raw scheduler string.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 09:33 and 09:38 UTC on 2026-06-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every eval pod that requests a remote agent VM times out unscheduled (~146–154 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream evidence collection impossible. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — if the remote VM pod cannot be scheduled, createAgent blocks and eventually times out, producing no evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared VM scheduling layer is the common dependency.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the kata peer-pod VM resource class have no remaining allocatable capacity, and no preemption victims exist to free slots. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. If those rules were recently tightened or if nodes were relabeled, the effective scheduling pool shrank to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, making capacity exhaustion more likely to surface.

TERTIARY — Insufficient cluster node count or VM quota for the kata peer-pod resource class: the cluster may have too few nodes provisioned with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to handle concurrent eval probes, or an upstream VM quota limit is preventing new peer-pod VMs from being allocated even when node capacity appears available.

LOW — Stale or leaked agent VMs from a prior eval run consuming the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if a previous probe run did not clean up its remote agent pods, those pods may still hold the VM resource allocation, leaving zero capacity for the current run.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify whether any stale or leaked eval pods are consuming the remaining VM slots that should have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agent VM Scheduling Layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the two nodes that carry this extended resource, blocking all remote agent pod creation. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks
affectedAreas.reason: remote-agent-create (required=true), remote-agent-state (required=true), and remote-agent-runtime (required=false) all failed with the same scheduling error, as registered at lines 183–185 of features.json. The feature is configured to degrade after 1 failure and declare outage after 2 failures (lines 187–188).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 1913–1918 calls createAgent() for a remote agent immediately after requireOrgId(). If the VM pod cannot be scheduled, createAgent() blocks until timeout and returns no evidence, causing a complete contract gap.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message, and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura'. All 5 fields are missing because the agent never started.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the two kata-capable cluster nodes immediately using kubectl describe node to confirm kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity and identify which pods are holding the remaining slots.
Audit the remote-agents namespace for stale or leaked eval pods that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs; terminate any orphaned pods to free VM slots.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted (not leaked), escalate to the infrastructure team to provision additional nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or increase the VM quota for the peer-pod resource class.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote agent pod spec to confirm that only the 2 kata-capable nodes are eligible and that no recent relabeling has further reduced the schedulable pool.

After restoring scheduling capacity, re-run all three remote-agents checks and confirm that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are present and that the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two kata-capable nodes shows available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or quota mechanism would need investigation.

If the node affinity/selector rules on the remote agent pod were recently changed to exclude the kata-capable nodes entirely (rather than the 4 non-kata nodes), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured affinity rule.

If a subsequent eval run with no other concurrent remote-agent workloads succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest the failure was caused by transient contention rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes while remote-agent-runtime continues to fail, it would indicate the scheduling layer recovered and the runtime failure has a different, downstream cause.

If other non-remote-agent checks in the same production-api environment also failed at the same time with unrelated errors, it could indicate a broader cluster disruption rather than a kata peer-pod-specific capacity issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on each eligible node and warns when available slots fall below a configured threshold, providing early warning before eval pods become unschedulable.

Add a stale-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than the eval timeout window and fails if any are found still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, catching cleanup failures from withCleanup.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures time-to-schedulable for a remote agent pod and warns at a threshold well below the 146–154 s timeout observed here, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent-runtime runner branch (run-status-probes.mjs) that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting createAgent(), and returns a distinct SKIP or WARN status with a capacity message rather than blocking until the full scheduler timeout.
